definitions.explanation: The act of offering incense at a Buddhist funeral, memorial service, or when visiting a grave. A key ritual in which mourners take turns approaching the altar to burn powdered incense.

examples.japanese: {順番|じゅんばん}に{焼香|しょうこう}した。
{葬儀|そうぎ}で{焼香|しょうこう}の{作法|さほう}がわからず{戸惑|とまど}った。
examples.english: I was flustered at the funeral because I didn't know the proper way to offer incense.

examples.japanese: {参列者|さんれつしゃ}が{一人|ひとり}ずつ{祭壇|さいだん}の{前|まえ}に{進|すす}み、{焼香|しょうこう}を{行|おこな}った。
examples.english: The attendees stepped forward one by one to the altar and offered incense.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
At Japanese Buddhist funerals and memorial services, {焼香|しょうこう} involves pinching powdered incense ({抹香|まっこう}) and sprinkling it onto a burner. The number of times one does this varies by Buddhist sect (typically one to three times). The etiquette can be confusing for younger Japanese and foreigners.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {焼香|しょうこう}する (to burn/offer incense)
- {焼香|しょうこう}を{上|あ}げる (to offer incense)
- {焼香|しょうこう}の{順番|じゅんばん} (the order of incense offering)
- {焼香|しょうこう}の{作法|さほう} (incense offering etiquette)
- {焼香|しょうこう}に{訪|おとず}れる (to visit to offer incense)

FORMS:
{焼|しょう} (to burn) + {香|こう} (incense).
